design_name: OOD decision utility of directed knowledge borrowing
post_existing_prediction_note: The underlying RMSE/R2 results were already known. No ranking, enrichment, first-hit, or regret result was inspected before this file was written. This is a post-outcome extension with prospectively locked decision endpoints, not an external preregistration.
scientific_question: Can a physically adjacent source prior improve decisions in the fixed out-of-distribution portion of a target experimental database even when average predictive fit is weak or unchanged?
estimand_scope: Retrospective finite-pool OOD screening utility under repeated target-label subsets; not population-wide causal generalization and not a prospective laboratory campaign.
candidate_direction: Higher target values are always preferred.

fixed_positive_definition.rule: Within each held-out candidate pool, the positive set is the first ceil(0.05*N) candidates after sorting by observed target value descending and material_key ascending.
fixed_positive_definition.tie_rule: The stable secondary key fixes the set size; ties are not expanded.

fixed_shortlist_definition.rule: The shortlist is the first ceil(0.10*N) candidates after sorting by prediction descending and material_key ascending.

primary_endpoint.name: candidate-pool fraction saved before the first top-5-percent hit
primary_endpoint.per_pool_baseline: one-indexed rank of the first true positive under baseline predictions divided by N
primary_endpoint.per_pool_augmented: one-indexed rank of the first true positive under augmented predictions divided by N
primary_endpoint.effect: baseline fraction minus augmented fraction; positive favors borrowing
primary_endpoint.fold_aggregation: Within each repeat, pool effects are weighted by candidate-pool size before inference.

secondary_endpoints: recall of true top-5-percent candidates inside the predicted top-10-percent shortlist
top-10-percent enrichment factor relative to random selection
simple regret after the predicted top-10-percent shortlist
Spearman rank correlation on the held-out candidate pool

primary_edges.ood_definition: chronological Year 1 to Year 2 and Years 1-2 to Year 3 held-out campaigns with zero canonical-composition overlap
outer folds hold out complete source articles; source models exclude held-out articles and exact held-out chemistries
official OBELiX evaluation groups with DOI/composition-disjoint target split and global removal of exact source-target composition overlap

secondary_boundaries.scope: within-campaign formulation holdout; positive reference, not independent OOD replication
official fold and exact-composition holdout; independent negative boundary but not labeled temporal or provenance OOD

inference.confidence_interval: paired percentile bootstrap over repeat identifiers
inference.raw_p_value: one-sided paired sign-flip Monte Carlo test over repeat-level effects with 9999 draws
inference.multiplicity: Holm correction across the three primary OOD edges only
inference.secondary_endpoints: descriptive and supportive; no separate significance claim

OOD_exploration_improvement: 95% bootstrap interval for the primary effect is entirely above zero
at least 80% of repeat-level effects are positive
relative reduction in mean fraction-to-first-hit is at least 25%
the named distant or shuffled controls do not pass all preceding gates
OOD_exploration_rescue: baseline median fraction-to-first-hit is greater than 0.10
augmented median fraction-to-first-hit is at most 0.10
decision_statuses.directional_only: primary point effect is positive but one or more improvement gates fail
decision_statuses.unresolved_or_harmful: primary point effect is non-positive or its interval is not bounded above zero

interpretive_guards: An OOD decision gain does not imply improved global RMSE or calibrated property prediction.
The fixed held-out database is a retrospective candidate pool, not a prospective experimental validation.
The first-hit endpoint evaluates ranking utility and cannot identify a microscopic mechanism.
Only the three named primary edges may support an independent OOD claim; KIT and Matbench are contextual boundaries.
A positive edge cannot be generalized into a universal transfer law.
